narr: A strong upper-level system brought widespread rounds of showers and thunderstorms to northwestern Connecticut on July 9-10, 2023. Northern and western portions of the county were hardest hit with rainfall amounts between 4 and 7 inches. This resulted in numerous reports of flash flooding and washed out roads and culverts.||A local declaration of emergency was issued in the Town of Norfolk following flash flood damage along Route 272. The damage along this road caused some homes to become isolated. A State of Emergency was also issued by Goshen First Selectman Todd Carusillo.
ev: Two houses were evacuated along Preston Mountain Road due to rising flood waters.
A culvert running under train tracks near the Town of Cornwall was washed out by flash flooding.
Multiple Roads were closed along the US Route 7 corridor as well as Schaghticoke Road from floodwaters caused by the swollen Housatonic River in the Town of Kent.
A section of Route 63 in Falls Village from Cobble Road to Barnes Road was closed due to flooding.

Several portions of Route 272 were washed out due to flash flooding between Bruey Road to Route 263 in Goshen. Numerous side roads were also closed including Smith Road, Old Goshen Road, Estey Road and Meekertown Road.
Only one lane was passable along portions of Colebrook River Road near Winsted due to flash flooding.
